problem_statement: Authors can choose which geometric side of a triangle is discarded during rasterization, but the engine still behaves as if “which winding counts as that side” were globally fixed. Content built with the opposite convention then disagrees with both conservative visibility and lighting that depend on front vs back, and mirrored hierarchies make the mismatch look like a transform bug rather than a raster rule bug. Make winding-order convention a real, user-visible rendering control: carry it on the shared material abstraction (including the usual persistence paths for standard materials), reflect it on the abstract graphics device for non-material code paths, and thread it through the same places that already establish face-related raster state for forward rendering and shadow casting. When the renderer already adjusts face-side behavior under negative scale, the new control must remain coherent with that adjustment. Each backend must apply the rule where its API actually fixes triangle orientation for rasterization, and any sharing of immutable GPU draw objects must not reuse a configuration that bakes in the wrong orientation between draws with different material settings.
problem_statement_variant: Sometimes the mesh is not “inside out” in the DCC package, yet here the silhouette and lighting disagree after mirroring or after certain imports—as if the engine silently picked a different notion of “outside” than the asset pipeline. Make that notion explicit, per material, end-to-end through the graphics stack, without breaking the cases that already worked.
hints: Trace how face-related raster state flows from scene draws into each backend; constants and device base types; concrete WebGL bootstrapping; WebGPU objects that describe triangle rasterization and how they are deduplicated; material copy paths; standard material ingestion; null-device tests for cheap verification.
